In [[mathematical logic]], the '''Barwise compactness theorem''', named after [[Jon Barwise]], is a generalization of the usual [[compactness theorem]] for [[first-order logic]] to a certain class of [[infinitary language]]s.  It was stated and proved by Barwise in 1967.

==Statement==

Let <math>A</math> be a countable [[admissible set]]. Let <math>L</math> be an <math>A</math>-finite relational [[Formal language|language]]. Suppose <math>\Gamma</math> is a set of <math>L_A</math>-sentences, where <math>\Gamma</math> is a <math>\Sigma_1</math> set with parameters from <math>A</math>, and every <math>A</math>-finite subset of <math>\Gamma</math> is [[Satisfiability|satisfiable]]. Then <math>\Gamma</math> is satisfiable.
